name: Joash
overview: Joash was a male king from the tribe of Judah, known specifically as the King of Judah and the son of Ahaziah. His reign and lineage are documented in 2 Kings 11:2 and 11:21. There are no additional notes beyond his royal status and familial connection.
namesAndTitles: Joash is also referred to as Jehoash, a name meaning 'YHWH bestows' or 'man of YHWH,' highlighting a connection to the Lord. His titles include 'King Jehoash' and 'King of Judah,' which affirm his royal authority and position as ruler of Judah during his lifetime.
familyAndRelationships: Joash was the son of Ahaziah and is inferred to have been the son of Zibiah as well. He had a nephew named Jehosheba. His masters included Jozacar and Jehozabad, who later killed him. Amaziah is also inferred as his father, indicating some complexity in his familial ties as recorded in Scripture.
scriptureSignificance: Joash's significance lies in his role as a king of Judah, continuing the Davidic line through his father Ahaziah. His reign is marked by interactions with key figures such as his masters Jozacar and Jehozabad, reflecting the political and spiritual challenges of his time. The biblical narrative recognizes him as a pivotal figure in Judah's monarchy, illustrating the ongoing covenantal history of God's people.
